chunks: And it was narrated from Abī al-Aswad al-Duʾalī:
That Muʿādh ibn Jabal was in Yemen, and people gathered around him and said: “A Jewish man has died and left behind a Muslim brother.”
So Muʿādh said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله say: ‘Islam increases and does not diminish.’” Thus he allowed the Muslim to inherit from his Jewish brother.

key_terms.أَخًا مُسْلِمًا: a Muslim brother, the heir mentioned in the case
key_terms.أَخِيهِ الْيَهُودِيِّ: his Jewish brother, the deceased relative from whom inheritance is given
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامُ: Islam, invoked here as the basis for the legal principle stated in the hadith
key_terms.فَوَرَّثَ: he gave inheritance; he ruled that the Muslim should inherit
key_terms.يَزِيدُ وَ لَا يَنْقُصُ: increases and does not diminish; a concise legal principle cited from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim inherit from a non-Muslim relative according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a ruling regarding inheritance between siblings of different religions. Muʿādh ibn Jabal cites the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم saying, “Islam increases and does not diminish,” and on that basis gives the Muslim brother inheritance from his Jewish brother.
